mira: heads up — a handful of model-serving pods in us-east1b are seeing connection drops and huge retransmit spikes, users report tail latency jumps. I can see repeated `conntrack: table full` in node syslogs.

sam: omg — which nodes? any pattern (gpu type / az)?

mira: nodes gpool-us-e1b-0[3-6] mostly, all A100s, RDMA-enabled overlay (recently flipped to improve perf).

ops-bot: ALERT: conntrack pressure on nodes gpool-us-e1b-03..06 — nf_conntrack_count=518312 nf_conntrack_max=524288 (threshold breached).

cheng: that nf_conntrack_count suggests we're exhausting the table. RDMA overlay + heavy ephemeral outbound SNATs from the prefetcher could be causing excessive tuples. Did we start any new batch prefetch jobs?

juan: we did roll out the model-prefetcher sidecar change yesterday that opens new connections per shard. Might be leaking connections or not reusing keepalives.

mira: quick mitigation — I'm going to bump nf_conntrack_max to 950000 on affected nodes and add a short conntrack prune cron while we debug. Doing via:
```
# on node
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=950000
echo 950000 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
```
This should stop immediate drops but we need a permanent fix.

sam: also lower some timeouts to free ESTABLISHED tuples faster? e.g.
```
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=120
```
Careful — that can break long-lived streams.

cheng: agree — short-term bump+prune is fine. Long-term: two prongs: 1) fix prefetcher to reuse keepalive TCP connections / use HTTP/2 multiplexing, 2) move away from node-wide SNAT to a pooled SNAT solution or eBPF-based NAT so we don't blow per-node conntrack.

juan: Yea, prefetcher change already fibered in branch, will push a canary that reuses keepalives and reduces ephemeral socket churn.

kim: I'll add a Grafana panel for `node:nf_conntrack_count:ratio` and an alert at 70% of nf_conntrack_max, plus a per-node ephemeral port usage heatmap (netstat ephemeral port ranges).

mira: rolling restart plan for the 4 nodes to reclaim state (respecting running jobs). Sam / Cheng — coordinate a controlled drain + uncordon window 10m each.

sam: starting cordon/drain on gpool-us-e1b-03 now. No job loss so far.

cheng: note — kernel 5.15 on these nodes has better conntrack performance with conntrack hashsize tuning. We should tune `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_hashsize` proportional to max tuples. Example:
```
echo 262144 > /sys/module/nf_conntrack/parameters/hashsize
```
We'll compute proper value after current burst subsides.

mira: also found this in node logs repeatedly: `nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet` around 12:03 UTC — exact time of spike aligns with a large model prefetch job kickoff.

juan: made prefetcher canary change to reuse keepalive, pushed to 10% of traffic for that pool. Early telemetry shows 60% fewer new TCP connections per minute.

cheng: ops followups:
- promote prefetcher fix to 100% after 12h validation
- implement per-node SNAT ip pool (reduce per-node tuple explosion) or enable CNI eBPF SNAT path
- add automated conntrack pruning job: `conntrack -L | grep TIME_WAIT | head -n 1000 | xargs -n1 -I{} conntrack -D {}` (careful, only after validation)
- run kernel upgrade plan (benefits later)

kim: I'll file a short runbook for future incidents (how to bump nf_conntrack_max safely, where to watch, dashboard links).

mira: thanks everyone — after bump + canary + node restarts the error counts fell back under 10/min. Keeping nodes in observability for next 24h.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident owner: mira.

mira: closing thread for now, will follow up with postmortem linking prefetcher change and config drift that removed keepalive.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: 1719009999 at 1719010875
